input.description: A boutique fitness studio wants a booking and membership platform. Members should be able to browse class schedules, book spots, manage their membership tier (drop-in, monthly, unlimited), and receive automated reminders. Studio staff need an admin view to manage classes, view attendance, and process refunds. Stripe for payments. The studio currently uses Mindbody but wants to move off it.

output:
## Recommended Stack

**Next.js** - This is an authenticated, transactional product with per-user dynamic state, server-side booking logic, and an admin layer. Next.js App Router handles all of this cleanly with server actions and API routes without reaching for a separate backend.

**Supabase** - Serves as the primary database (Postgres), file storage, and real-time layer. Row-level security policies tie directly to membership tiers and booking permissions, which is exactly the kind of data-access control this platform needs. Supabase Auth is the natural choice here given the full Supabase stack.

**Supabase Auth** - The project is already on the full Supabase stack, and RLS policies need to tie auth directly to database-level access - for example, ensuring members can only see and cancel their own bookings, and staff can access admin views. This is the correct auth choice here, not Clerk.

**shadcn/ui** - Provides the accessible, composable component foundation for both the member-facing UI and the staff admin view. Tailwind CSS is included as part of this setup. Components like calendars, modals, and data tables are available out of the box and can be styled to match the studio's brand without fighting a design system.

**Stripe** - Handles all payment flows: one-off drop-in purchases, recurring monthly subscriptions, and unlimited plan billing. Stripe's customer portal handles subscription management and reduces the amount of custom billing UI the team needs to build. Stripe webhooks drive membership status updates in Supabase in real time.

**Resend** - Manages transactional email: booking confirmations, cancellation notices, and automated class reminders. Pairs cleanly with Next.js server actions and is significantly more reliable and developer-friendly than configuring raw SMTP or a legacy provider like SendGrid.

**Vercel** - Deploys the Next.js application with zero-config CI/CD, edge caching, and preview environments per branch. The right hosting choice for a Next.js project at this scale.

---

## Phase Breakdown

| Phase | Description | Est. Weeks | Est. Cost (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discovery | Audit the client's current Mindbody data and export formats, map membership tiers and business rules, define class scheduling logic, confirm Stripe billing model, and align on admin workflow requirements. | 2 | $3,000-$5,000 |
| Design | UX and UI design for member-facing flows (schedule browse, booking, account management) and staff admin views (class management, attendance, refunds). Includes a design system grounded in the studio's brand. | 3-4 | $8,000-$12,000 |
| Development | Build and integrate all features: auth, class scheduling, booking engine with capacity management, membership tier logic, Stripe subscriptions and payments, automated reminders, admin dashboard, and Mindbody data migration. | 8-10 | $22,000-$28,000 |
| QA & Launch | End-to-end testing of booking and payment flows, cross-browser and mobile-responsive QA, staff training on admin view, data migration validation, and staged production launch. | 2-3 | $4,000-$5,000 |

---

## Technical Risks

1. **Mindbody data migration is unpredictable.** Mindbody's data export capabilities are notoriously inconsistent - member records, booking history, and subscription states may not export cleanly. Discovery must include a hands-on audit of what data is actually exportable before any migration timeline is committed to. Budget for manual data cleaning.

2. **Stripe subscription and membership state getting out of sync.** If a webhook fails or is processed out of order, a member's tier in Supabase can drift from their actual Stripe subscription status. This needs a robust webhook handler with idempotency keys, retry logic, and a reconciliation mechanism - not a naive fire-and-forget implementation.

3. **Booking concurrency and class capacity edge cases.** Two members booking the last spot simultaneously is a classic race condition. This must be handled at the database level using Postgres transactions or row-level locking - not application-level checks, which will fail under real load.

4. **Scope creep from replacing a feature-heavy platform.** Mindbody does a lot - waitlists, late cancellation penalties, instructor management, retail POS, and more. The client may not realise how many implicit features they rely on until they no longer have them. Discovery must produce an explicit feature inventory and a clear line between in-scope and out-of-scope functionality before development starts.

5. **Automated reminder timing logic across timezones.** If the studio has members or classes spanning timezones, reminder scheduling becomes non-trivial. Even for a single-timezone studio, daylight saving transitions can cause reminders to fire at the wrong time. This should be handled using UTC storage and a reliable job scheduler - Supabase's pg_cron or a lightweight queue - not ad hoc setTimeout logic.

---

## Suggested Team

- **Project Manager** - Owns timeline, client communication, and keeps Discovery findings from expanding scope uncontrollably.
- **UI/UX Designer** - Designs member-facing flows and admin views, with particular attention to the booking experience on mobile.
- **Full-Stack Developer (Lead)** - Owns the Next.js application architecture, Supabase schema, Stripe integration, and booking engine logic.
- **Full-Stack Developer (Support)** - Builds admin dashboard, email automation, and assists with data migration scripting.
- **QA Engineer** - Owns end-to-end test coverage for booking and payment flows, and validates migrated data integrity pre-launch.

---

## Assumptions & Exclusions

**Assumptions**
- The client can provide access to their Mindbody account and an export of member and booking data during Discovery.
- The studio operates in a single timezone.
- Membership tiers are limited to the three described: drop-in, monthly, and unlimited. Additional tiers or hybrid pricing models are out of scope.
- The client will provide brand assets (logo, typography, colour palette) before Design begins.
- Stripe has been or can be set up under the client's own business account - the agency is not responsible for Stripe onboarding or KYC.
- Class scheduling is managed by studio staff via the admin view - there is no automated or AI-driven scheduling requirement.
- The platform is web-only; no native iOS or Android app is required.

**Exclusions**
- Native mobile applications (iOS or Android).
- A native waitlist feature (can be scoped as a post-launch addition).
- Late cancellation fee automation or penalty logic.
- Instructor-facing portals or instructor payroll management.
- Retail or merchandise point-of-sale functionality.
- Multilingual or multi-currency support.
- Multi-location support (this scope covers a single studio location).
- Ongoing content updates or class schedule population after launch.
- Post-launch support and maintenance retainer (available under a separate agreement).

---

## Post-Launch Costs

- **Vercel Pro** - $20/month - Covers production deployments, preview environments, and usage within a reasonable traffic band for a single studio.
- **Supabase Pro** - $25/month - Includes 8GB database, 100GB storage, 5GB bandwidth, and daily backups. Essential for a production application handling real member and payment data.
- **Resend** - $0-$20/month - Free tier covers up to 3,000 emails/month; paid plan needed if reminder and confirmation volume exceeds that. Realistic for an active studio.
- **Stripe** - 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction - No monthly fee, but this is a real cost the client should factor into class and membership pricing. Subscription billing incurs an additional 0.5% per recurring charge.

**Estimated total infrastructure cost: $45-$65/month** at launch scale, excluding Stripe transaction fees.

---

## Recommended Next Steps

1. **Schedule a Mindbody audit session with the client this week.** Request admin access or a full data export to assess what member records, booking history, and subscription data are actually recoverable. This single step will determine whether migration is a two-day script or a multi-week project - and it must be resolved before the proposal is finalised.

2. **Present this scope in a working session and walk through the Exclusions list explicitly.** Mindbody users are accustomed to features like waitlists and late cancellation penalties. Getting the client to sign off on what is not included before contracts are signed is the single most effective way to prevent scope disputes mid-project.

3. **Prepare a phased contract structure with Discovery as a separate, fixed-fee engagement.** Given the migration uncertainty and the risk of undiscovered Mindbody dependencies, propose Discovery as a standalone $3,000-$5,000 fixed engagement that produces a detailed feature inventory and migration plan. The full build contract is then signed off that document - protecting both the agency and the client from budget surprises.

input.description: I am a Pokemon collector who invests in elite trainer boxes and individual cards and I often check multiple sources, like e-bay and tcgplayer, to find the current market value and average price of my investments, to see how much they have increased in value. I want to build an app that allows me add my portfolio items and provides real time up to date data and prices for all relevant sources. It is simple, I want to visit the app and see my investments. and then add any future investments as I get them. I want a sleek and modern design and each item to have a picture and all relevant details. I want to see the date that I added the item and the average price across all platforms. there should be a list of all items and each item should have their own page with more details.

output:
## Recommended Stack

**Next.js (App Router)** - This is an authenticated, data-driven portfolio app with per-user state, API routes for price fetching, and dynamic item pages. Next.js is the right foundation - App Router gives you server components for fast initial loads and server actions for clean data mutations.

**Supabase** - Handles your database, file storage (card and box images), and auth in one platform. For a solo founder at this scale, Supabase eliminates the need to manage separate services and its free tier will comfortably cover early usage. Row-level security ensures each user only ever sees their own portfolio data.

**Supabase Auth** - You're already on the full Supabase stack, and auth ties directly to RLS policies at the database level. This means your portfolio data is protected by design, not just by application logic. No per-MAU pricing surprises as your user base grows.

**shadcn/ui** - Gives you a polished, modern component library out of the box - cards, tables, modals, and detail pages all built on accessible primitives with Tailwind CSS baked in. You get a professional UI without designing from scratch.

**TanStack Query** - Manages server state, caching, and background refetching for your price data. When you load your portfolio, prices stay fresh without manual refresh logic - critical when you're pulling from multiple external sources.

**eBay Browse API + TCGPlayer API** - These are the two primary data sources for real-time market pricing. Both have public or partner-level API access. eBay's Browse API returns sold listing data; TCGPlayer provides market price and low/mid/high ranges. These will be called server-side via Next.js API routes to protect your API keys.

**Vercel** - The natural deployment target for Next.js. Zero-config deploys, edge caching for your price fetch routes, and a generous free tier to start. You can be live in minutes.

---

## Phase Breakdown

| Phase | Description | Est. Weeks |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery | Define the full data model (cards vs. ETBs, which fields matter), confirm API access and rate limits for eBay and TCGPlayer, map out the portfolio views and item detail page structure. | 1 |
| Design | Design the portfolio list view, item detail page, add-item flow, and empty states. Establish the visual language - dark/light mode preference, card imagery layout, price display hierarchy. | 1-2 |
| Development | Build auth and user accounts, Supabase schema and RLS, image upload, portfolio CRUD, eBay and TCGPlayer API integrations, price aggregation logic, list view, and individual item pages. | 4-6 |
| QA & Launch | Cross-browser and mobile testing, API error handling and fallback states, performance review, Vercel production deploy. | 1 |

---

## Technical Risks

1. **TCGPlayer API access is not guaranteed.** TCGPlayer's public API has been increasingly restricted - full programmatic access may require a formal partner agreement or be unavailable entirely. Validate this in week one before designing around it. A fallback is scraping or using a community-maintained price dataset, but both carry reliability and legal risks.

2. **eBay sold listing data requires careful filtering.** Raw eBay API results include listings in wildly different conditions, languages, and bundle configurations. Without strict filtering logic, your average price calculations will be meaningless. This needs deliberate engineering - not just a raw average of returned results.

3. **Price aggregation across platforms is harder than it looks.** eBay and TCGPlayer price different things - eBay reflects recent sale prices, TCGPlayer reflects current listings. Presenting a single "average price" that is honest and useful requires a clear methodology. You need to decide this upfront, or the numbers will mislead you.

4. **Image management at scale can get messy.** Storing card and box images in Supabase Storage is straightforward early on, but if you plan to open this to other collectors, storage and bandwidth costs grow quickly. Consider whether you want to pull official card images from a public database like Pokémon TCG API rather than uploading manually - this would also improve data consistency.

5. **This is a solo build - scope creep is the biggest risk.** "ASAP" timelines and undefined budgets on feature-rich apps are a classic trap. The MVP should be: add an item, see a price, view a list. Everything else - charts, price history, alerts - is phase two. Ship the core loop first.

---

## Suggested Team

**Full-Stack Developer** - Owns the entire build: Next.js frontend, Supabase backend, API integrations, and deployment. This is a solo-buildable product if you have the skills or hire one strong generalist.

**UI/UX Designer** - Defines the visual design, component structure, and interaction patterns. Can be a short engagement (2-3 weeks) rather than a full-time hire. If budget is tight, shadcn/ui defaults get you far with minimal design input.

**You (Founder)** - Owns product decisions, API partnership outreach (especially TCGPlayer), and acceptance testing. Your domain knowledge as a collector is the most valuable input in shaping what data actually matters.

---

## Assumptions & Exclusions

**Assumptions**
- You have or can obtain API access to both eBay and TCGPlayer before development begins
- The initial version is for your personal use only - not a multi-user SaaS product
- Card and box images can either be uploaded manually or pulled from the Pokémon TCG API (free, public)
- "Real-time" pricing means fetched on page load or on a short cache interval (e.g. every few hours) - not a live streaming feed
- You are comfortable managing a Supabase project and Vercel deployment with basic technical guidance

**Exclusions**
- Native iOS or Android app - this is a web app only
- Price history charts or trend tracking over time (phase two feature)
- Push notifications or price alert emails
- Automated portfolio valuation reports or exports
- Support for non-Pokémon TCG products (other card games, other collectibles)
- Any integration beyond eBay and TCGPlayer (e.g. PWCC, Whatnot, CardMarket)
- Content creation - card descriptions, set information, or editorial copy
- Post-launch maintenance or ongoing support

---

## Post-Launch Costs

**Vercel (Hobby/Pro)** - $0-$20/month - Free tier covers personal projects comfortably; Pro needed if you add collaborators or need higher build limits.

**Supabase** - $0-$25/month - Free tier handles the database, auth, and storage for a single-user portfolio app. Pro plan needed if storage or API usage grows significantly.

**eBay Developer Program** - $0/month - API access is free at standard call volumes for approved developer accounts.

**TCGPlayer API** - $0-$unknown/month - Pricing depends on partnership tier; this is the one cost that cannot be estimated until you have a confirmed agreement with them.

**Pokémon TCG API (if used for card images)** - $0/month - Fully free and open for non-commercial use.

Estimated total at launch scale: **$0-$45/month** excluding any TCGPlayer API fees.

---

## Recommended Next Steps

1. **Validate TCGPlayer API access this week.** Go to the TCGPlayer developer portal and apply for API access now. This is the single biggest technical unknown in the project - everything else can be built around it, but you need to know what you're working with before writing a line of code.

2. **Sketch your ideal portfolio list view and item detail page on paper or Figma.** You know better than anyone what data matters to you as a collector. Write down every field you want to see on the list (name, set, purchase price, current value, date added) and on the item detail page. This becomes the data model and saves hours of back-and-forth in development.

3. **Spin up a Supabase project and a Next.js app locally and get a single hardcoded card rendering on screen.** This is your technical spike - it proves the stack works, gets you familiar with the tools, and gives you something real to look at within a day. Momentum matters on solo builds.

input.description: A boutique fitness studio wants a booking and membership platform. Members should be able to browse class schedules, book spots, manage their membership tier (drop-in, monthly, unlimited), and receive automated reminders. Studio staff need an admin view to manage classes, view attendance, and process refunds. Stripe for payments. The studio currently uses Mindbody but wants to move off it.

output:
## Recommended Stack

**Next.js** - This is an authenticated, transactional product with per-user dynamic state, server-side booking logic, and an admin layer. Next.js App Router gives us API routes, server actions, and a clean separation between member-facing and staff-facing surfaces in a single codebase.

**Supabase** - Serves as the primary backend: PostgreSQL database, Row Level Security to enforce that members only access their own bookings and membership data, and real-time subscriptions for live class capacity updates. Supabase Auth is the natural choice here given the full Supabase stack - RLS policies tie directly to auth identity, which is exactly what a booking platform needs at the data layer.

**Supabase Auth** - Members and staff authenticate through Supabase Auth, with RLS policies enforcing data access at the database level. Role-based access (member vs. staff vs. admin) is handled cleanly through Postgres roles without introducing a second auth vendor.

**shadcn/ui** - Component foundation built on Tailwind CSS. Gives the team a complete, accessible set of UI primitives - dialogs, calendars, data tables, form controls - that are essential for a booking interface and admin dashboard without building from scratch.

**Stripe** - Handles all payment flows: one-time drop-in purchases, recurring monthly subscriptions, and unlimited tier billing. Stripe's subscription management and webhook infrastructure also drives membership state changes in the database, and the refund API covers the staff-side refund requirement directly.

**Resend** - Transactional email for automated booking confirmations, class reminders, cancellation notices, and membership renewal alerts. Reliable deliverability with a developer-friendly API that integrates cleanly with Next.js server actions and Supabase Edge Functions.

**Supabase Edge Functions** - Scheduled and event-driven background logic: processing Stripe webhooks to update membership status, triggering reminder emails 24 hours before a class, and handling waitlist promotion when a spot opens. Keeps background jobs inside the existing Supabase infrastructure rather than introducing a separate queue service.

---

## Phase Breakdown

| Phase | Description | Est. Weeks | Est. Cost (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discovery | Audit the Mindbody data export, map existing class structures and membership tiers, define booking rules (cancellation windows, waitlists, capacity limits), document staff workflows, and finalise technical requirements before a line of code is written. | 2-3 | $6,000-$10,000 |
| Design | UX and UI for member-facing flows (schedule browse, booking, account management) and the staff admin dashboard. Includes mobile-responsive design, component library setup, and client sign-off before development begins. | 3-4 | $10,000-$16,000 |
| Development | Full build: authentication, class scheduling engine, booking and waitlist logic, Stripe subscription and payment flows, admin dashboard (class management, attendance, refunds), automated reminders, and Mindbody data migration. | 8-12 | $28,000-$52,000 |
| QA & Launch | End-to-end testing of booking flows and payment scenarios, load testing class capacity logic, staff UAT, Stripe webhook validation, and a staged rollover from Mindbody with a defined cutover plan. | 2-3 | $6,000-$12,000 |

---

## Technical Risks

1. **Mindbody data migration is the highest-risk item in this project.** Mindbody's data export is notoriously inconsistent - member histories, class records, and recurring billing data may not export cleanly. A dedicated discovery spike to assess the actual export quality is non-negotiable before committing to migration timelines.

2. **Stripe subscription and database state can diverge.** If a webhook is missed or processed out of order, a member's tier in the database won't match what Stripe holds as truth. Idempotent webhook handling and a reconciliation job that periodically syncs Stripe subscription status to the database must be built into the architecture from day one - not retrofitted.

3. **Booking concurrency under class capacity limits is harder than it looks.** Two members booking the last spot simultaneously is a classic race condition. This must be handled with Postgres row-level locking or a serialised transaction pattern in Supabase - optimistic UI updates alone will cause overselling.

4. **Scope creep from the Mindbody feature set.** Mindbody is a decade-old product with hundreds of features the studio may not consciously use but will miss once they're gone. Discovery must produce an explicit feature parity list with agreed inclusions and exclusions, signed off by the client, before development starts.

5. **Automated reminder timing logic is deceptively complex.** Class times, timezones, cancellation windows, and reminder schedules interact in ways that produce subtle bugs. The studio's local timezone must be treated as a first-class configuration value, and all scheduling logic should be tested against daylight saving transitions explicitly.

---

## Suggested Team

- **Project Manager** - Owns timeline, client communication, sprint ceremonies, and the Mindbody migration coordination.
- **UI/UX Designer** - Leads all design phases from user flows through to production-ready components, with particular attention to the mobile booking experience.
- **Lead Full-Stack Engineer** - Owns the Next.js application architecture, booking and concurrency logic, Stripe integration, and Supabase schema design.
- **Full-Stack Engineer** - Builds the admin dashboard, Edge Function jobs, email flows, and supports the member-facing feature build.
- **QA Engineer** - Owns test planning, booking flow automation, Stripe webhook scenario testing, and coordinates staff UAT ahead of cutover.

---

## Assumptions & Exclusions

**Assumptions**
- The client can export usable member, class, and transaction data from Mindbody in a structured format (CSV or API) during Discovery.
- The studio operates in a single timezone and a single currency (USD).
- Membership tiers are limited to the three described: drop-in, monthly, and unlimited. Additional tiers are out of scope unless agreed in Discovery.
- The client will provide brand assets, logo files, and a defined colour palette before the Design phase begins.
- Staff admin users will be a small, known set (under 20 users) - no self-serve staff onboarding is required.
- The client has an active Stripe account or is able to create one before Development begins.
- Class scheduling follows a repeating weekly template with occasional one-off additions - no AI-generated or algorithmically optimised scheduling is required.
- A single web application covers both mobile and desktop via responsive design. A native iOS or Android app is not in scope.

**Exclusions**
- Native mobile applications (iOS or Android).
- A public-facing marketing or brand website - this scope covers the booking and membership platform only.
- Integration with any third-party fitness hardware, wearables, or heart rate tracking systems.
- Multi-location support - this platform is scoped for a single studio location.
- Multilingual or multi-currency support.
- In-person point-of-sale or hardware terminal integration.
- Ongoing content creation, class photography, or copywriting.
- Post-launch support and maintenance retainer (to be scoped separately).
- Any Mindbody API integration - migration is a one-time data transfer, not a live sync.

---

## Post-Launch Costs

- **Supabase Pro** - $25/month - Covers the production database, auth, Edge Functions, and storage with sufficient headroom for a single-studio operation.
- **Vercel Pro** - $20/month - Hosts the Next.js application with preview deployments, analytics, and the performance headroom a transactional app needs over the free tier.
- **Stripe** - 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction - No flat monthly fee, but payment processing costs scale directly with revenue. Subscription billing is included. Budget accordingly based on expected monthly transaction volume.
- **Resend** - $0-$20/month - Free tier covers 3,000 emails/month. A studio with active members will likely stay within the $20/month plan (50,000 emails) for the foreseeable future.

**Estimated total infrastructure cost at launch scale: $45-$65/month** (excluding Stripe transaction fees).

---

## Recommended Next Steps

1. **Request a Mindbody data export immediately and assess its quality.** Ask the client to initiate a full data export from Mindbody this week - member records, class history, attendance, and transaction data. The shape and completeness of that export will directly determine migration complexity and may affect the project timeline and budget before a contract is signed.

2. **Run a two-hour booking rules workshop with the studio owner and a senior staff member.** Cancellation windows, waitlist behaviour, no-show policies, refund rules, and membership freeze logic are all decisions that must be locked before design begins. Surface these in a structured session and document the outcomes as a decision log that becomes part of the contract scope.

3. **Present this scope with a phased contract structure - Discovery as a separate, fixed-fee engagement.** Given the Mindbody migration risk and the likelihood of undiscovered complexity in the booking rules, propose that the client signs a fixed-fee Discovery phase first ($6,000-$10,000) before committing to the full build budget. This protects both parties and produces a detailed specification that makes the remaining phases far more predictable to price.

- A native mobile app or push notification system. Email reminders via Resend are included; SMS is not.
- Integration with any third-party fitness hardware, wearables, or heart rate platforms.
- A public-facing marketing or brand website. This scope covers the booking and membership platform only.
- Multilingual or multi-currency support.
- Multi-location support. This scope is for a single studio location.
- Ongoing content management by non-technical staff beyond class scheduling (e.g. blog, editorial content).
- Post-launch maintenance, hosting management, or feature development beyond the agreed scope.

---

## Post-Launch Costs

- **Vercel Pro** - $20/month - Covers production hosting, CI/CD pipelines, and preview environments for any future development work.
- **Supabase Pro** - $25/month - Includes 8GB database, 100GB storage, and daily backups. Sufficient for a single-studio platform at launch scale.
- **Stripe** - 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction - No monthly fee; cost scales directly with revenue. Subscription billing is included at no additional platform charge.
- **Resend** - $0-$20/month - Free tier covers 3,000 emails/month. A moderately active studio with automated reminders will likely stay within the $20 Pro tier.

**Estimated total monthly infrastructure cost: $45-$65/month** (excluding Stripe transaction fees, which scale with revenue).

---

## Recommended Next Steps

1. **Request a Mindbody data export and access audit this week.** Ask the client to pull a full export of member records, booking history, and class data from Mindbody. Review the format and completeness before Discovery kicks off - this single item has the most potential to affect timeline and cost, and you need to know what you're dealing with before the contract is signed.

2. **Run a 90-minute Discovery scoping session with the studio owner and a staff member who uses Mindbody daily.** The goal is to document every Mindbody feature they currently use, identify which are genuinely needed versus habit, and get verbal agreement on what is out of scope. Record the session. This becomes the foundation for the feature sign-off document that protects the agency from scope creep.

3. **Send a proposal with a clearly gated Discovery phase as the first commercial milestone.** Structure the contract so Discovery is a paid, fixed-fee engagement that produces a finalised feature list and migration strategy. This protects the agency if the Mindbody data situation turns out to be more complex than expected, and gives the client a natural decision point before the full build budget is committed.

## Recommended Stack

**Google Docs / Notion** - All three deliverables are strategy and reference documents, not software. A shared Notion workspace gives the client a living, navigable home for the audit summary, strategy document, and governance guide - easy to update and hand off without any technical overhead.

**Figma** - Used to produce any visual direction slides, content pillar frameworks, or channel strategy layouts that need to be designed rather than written. Keeps everything presentation-ready without committing to a heavier tool.

**Airtable** - A lightweight content audit tracker to log current social posts, cadence, engagement patterns, and gaps across 4-5 platforms during Phase 1. Shareable with the client and reusable as an ongoing content calendar template post-engagement.

**Rival IQ or Sprout Social (audit-only access)** - Provides competitive benchmarking and engagement data during the audit phase without requiring a full platform subscription. Justifies strategic recommendations with real performance data rather than observation alone.

---

## Phase Breakdown

| Phase | Description | Est. Weeks | Est. Cost (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discovery | Stakeholder working sessions, review of brand and content strategy assets, social media audit across 4-5 platforms, synthesis of findings into Audit & Insights Summary | 2-3 weeks | $2,500-$3,500 |
| Strategy Development | Define strategic framework, objectives, KPIs, audience priorities, content pillars, and full channel strategies for 4-5 platforms. Produce Social Media Strategy Document | 2-3 weeks | $3,500-$4,500 |
| Governance Guide & QA | Develop the Social Media Governance Guide covering voice, tone, visual direction, guardrails, and workflow. Internal review, client feedback round, and final revisions across all deliverables | 1-2 weeks | $1,500-$2,000 |

---

## Technical Risks

1. **Stakeholder alignment takes longer than scoped.** Social media strategy often surfaces disagreements between marketing, brand, and executive stakeholders about audience priorities or channel investment. Build one structured working session into Discovery and set a clear sign-off process before Phase 2 begins - otherwise feedback loops will blow the timeline.

2. **Access to meaningful performance data may be limited.** If the client cannot provide admin-level access to social accounts or historical analytics exports, the audit will rely on surface-level observations. Confirm data access in the first week - this directly affects the quality of the Audit & Insights Summary.

3. **Scope of "4-5 platforms" is undefined.** LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok each require meaningfully different strategic treatment. If the client expects deep channel strategies for five platforms within this budget, something will be thin. Agree on the priority platform list before Phase 2 begins and document it.

4. **Deliverables may be treated as a starting point for expanded work.** Strategy documents frequently generate requests for execution support, content creation, or paid social planning that are outside this scope. Be explicit in the proposal about what is and is not included to avoid unpaid scope creep post-delivery.

5. **Brand and content strategy assets may not exist in a usable form.** The brief assumes the client has documented brand strategy, messaging frameworks, and content strategy to review. If these are incomplete or inconsistent, Phase 1 will take longer and the social strategy will rest on shakier foundations. Flag this risk early and agree on what "good enough" looks like.

---

## Suggested Team

- **Strategy Lead** - Owns the overall engagement, leads stakeholder sessions, and is accountable for the quality and coherence of all three deliverables.
- **Social Media Strategist** - Conducts the platform audit, develops content pillars and channel strategies, and drafts the Governance Guide.
- **Designer** - Produces any visual frameworks, channel strategy layouts, or presentation-ready versions of deliverables in Figma.
- **Project Manager** - Manages timeline, client communication, feedback rounds, and keeps the engagement on budget.

---

## Assumptions & Exclusions

**Assumptions**
- The client will provide access to existing brand strategy, content strategy, and messaging framework documents at the start of Phase 1.
- The client will grant analytics access or export historical performance data for all priority social accounts.
- A maximum of two rounds of consolidated client feedback are included across all deliverables.
- The client will identify and make available the relevant internal stakeholders for the Discovery working session within the first week of the engagement.
- Priority platforms (4-5) will be agreed and locked before Phase 2 begins.
- All deliverables are written in English only.

**Exclusions**
- Content creation, copywriting, or social post production of any kind.
- Paid social strategy, media planning, or ad creative recommendations.
- Community management guidance or crisis communications playbooks.
- Influencer or creator partnership strategy.
- Implementation, scheduling, or ongoing management of social channels.
- Any software development, tool configuration, or platform integrations.
- SEO, email, or other channel strategies beyond social media.
- Post-engagement retainer or execution support.

---

## Post-Launch Costs

- **Notion (Team plan)** - $16-$20/month - Hosts and maintains the living strategy and governance documents for the client's team post-handoff.
- **Airtable (Plus plan)** - $10-$20/month - Keeps the content audit tracker and any content calendar template usable and shareable across the client's social team.
- **Sprout Social or equivalent publishing tool** - $99-$249/month - If the client wants to act on cadence and workflow recommendations, a social management platform will be needed. This is the client's decision and cost to own.

**Estimated total post-launch overhead: $125-$290/month**, depending on whether the client adopts a social management platform.

---

## Recommended Next Steps

1. **Send the client a pre-kickoff asset request this week.** Draft a short checklist requesting brand strategy documents, existing content strategy, messaging frameworks, and social account analytics access. Getting this in motion before contracts are signed surfaces any data gaps early and signals the agency's rigour from day one.

2. **Confirm the priority platform list with the client before finalising the proposal.** Request a 30-minute call or async response to lock in which 4-5 platforms are in scope. This single decision has the biggest impact on Phase 2 effort and should be documented in the signed agreement - not left open.

3. **Define the feedback and approval process in the contract.** Specify that each deliverable includes one draft and two rounds of consolidated written feedback, and that sign-off is required before the next phase begins. This protects the timeline and budget, and sets professional expectations before work starts.
